method: Independent direct visual inspection of actual PNG renders, decoded via System.Drawing; QA ENGINEER provides interaction and timing evidence separately.
provenance: Final candidate refreshed screenshots confirmed by QA ENGINEER and visible field downshift / aligned C receiver. report.json shots and capture-report.json are authoritative. Older candidate1 1280 A/B images are excluded from this verdict.

criteria.question: Is source obvious?
criteria.evidence: Bright cyan aperture visibly begins thick cyan beam; source has distinct horizontal barrel.

criteria.question: Is receiver obvious?
criteria.evidence: Inactive dark target has cyan rim, distinct from silver diagonal mirrors; successful target becomes bright white cyan.

criteria.question: Is beam clearly visible?
criteria.evidence: Bright core and dark contrast edge remain dominant against lab; partial and complete route directly inspected.

criteria.question: Can child tell which objects rotate?
criteria.evidence: Large directional silver faces visibly change diagonal orientation; no objectionable crop seam observed.

criteria.question: Does every tap visibly change beam?
criteria.evidence: Reached mirrors visibly change the route in reviewed initial/partial/complete states. An unreached downstream mirror rotates visibly but cannot physically change the upstream beam. Rapid input and immediate orientation response are covered by QA ENGINEER report, not inferred from screenshots.

criteria.question: Is robot part of scene?
criteria.evidence: Robot stands beside apparatus away from edge, feet grounded in initial states; raised celebration pose seen in completed phone frame.

criteria.question: Is puzzle centered on platform?
criteria.evidence: Final apparatus groups around platform rear and front within bounded central composition; 1920 desktop does not spread across full width.

criteria.question: Is there no redundant explanatory text?
criteria.evidence: Single safe centered title; progress below it; gameplay unobstructed by explanatory or persistent feedback text.

criteria.question: Does success feel satisfying?
criteria.evidence: Complete bright route, active receiver, cyan path pulse, restored platform lights and robot celebration visible. Perceived real-device timing and child response remain for physical review.

resolvedFindings: Baseline had no obvious beam and scattered objects / edge robot; final screenshots clearly communicate linked apparatus.
Candidate1 upper apparatus was too high over bench/window; final centralized downward shift and aligned C receiver improve platform anchoring.
Early receiver-activated captures accidentally showed Launch due capture latency; final 844C and 1280C activated screenshots directly verified as SIGNAL with lit receiver and pulse.
limitations: No physical Samsung or child usability session performed.
Screenshot review cannot establish instant response, sound, or full temporal celebration; interaction QA is separate.
Literal beam change on every downstream unreached mirror tap is not supported; visible rotation is the feedback in that physically unchanged path state.

rootAdditionalReview.method: Direct image inspection; desktop/tablet images downsampled only in memory for viewing.
rootAdditionalReview.notes: Beam remains prominent, apparatus is bounded around the platform, robot is grounded/inward in initial states, tablet and wide desktop have no visible HUD or apparatus overlap.
